From 42c1a6f62e5c46269ed37238f6a5331b30c32c75 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Marek Vasut <marex@denx.de>
Date: Tue, 26 Apr 2022 22:03:29 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] arm64: dts: imx8mm: Use 100 kHz I2C2 on Data Modul i.MX8M
 Mini eDM SBC

The I2C2 has SMBus device SMSC USB2514Bi connected to it, the device is
capable of up to 100 kHz operation. Reduce the bus frequency to 100 kHz
to guarantee this I2C device can work correctly.

Fixes: 583f24ae42a07 ("arm64: dts: imx8mm: Add support for Data Modul i.MX8M Mini eDM SBC")
Signed-off-by: Marek Vasut <marex@denx.de>
Cc: Fabio Estevam <festevam@denx.de>
Cc: Peng Fan <peng.fan@nxp.com>
Cc: Shawn Guo <shawnguo@kernel.org>
Cc: NXP Linux Team <linux-imx@nxp.com>
To: linux-arm-kernel@lists.infradead.org
Signed-off-by: Shawn Guo <shawnguo@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/freescale/imx8mm-data-modul-edm-sbc.dts b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/freescale/imx8mm-data-modul-edm-sbc.dts
index b2d90b79f500..8c9dd09dbc74 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/freescale/imx8mm-data-modul-edm-sbc.dts
+++ b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/freescale/imx8mm-data-modul-edm-sbc.dts
@@ -392,7 +392,7 @@ ldo6_reg: LDO6 {
 
 &i2c2 {
 	/* IMX8MM ERRATA e7805 -- I2C is limited to 384 kHz due to SoC bug */
-	clock-frequency = <320000>;
+	clock-frequency = <100000>;
 	pinctrl-names = "default", "gpio";
 	pinctrl-0 = <&pinctrl_i2c2>;
 	pinctrl-1 = <&pinctrl_i2c2_gpio>;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm64/boot/dts/freescale/imx8mm-data-modul-edm-sbc.dts`**
   - The `clock-frequency` property for the I2C2 node has been changed from `320000` (320 kHz) to `100000` (100 kHz). This modification ensures that the I2C2 bus operates at a frequency compatible with the connected SMBus device, SMSC USB2514Bi, which can only function correctly at up to 100 kHz.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change in the `clock-frequency` for I2C2 directly addresses the compatibility issue with the SMSC USB2514Bi device. By reducing the frequency from 320 kHz to 100 kHz, the patch resolves potential operational issues that could arise from exceeding the device's maximum frequency capability. This modification is a corrective action following a previous commit (identified by the fix reference) that added support for the Data Modul i.MX8M Mini eDM SBC, indicating that the initial configuration was not suitable for the hardware setup.

Here is the commit message:
arm64: dts: imx8mm: Use 100 kHz I2C2 on Data Modul i.MX8M
 Mini eDM SBC

The I2C2 has SMBus device SMSC USB2514Bi connected to it, the device is
capable of up to 100 kHz operation. Reduce the bus frequency to 100 kHz
to guarantee this I2C device can work correctly.

Fixes: 583f24ae42a07 ("arm64: dts: imx8mm: Add support for Data Modul i.MX8M Mini eDM SBC")
Signed-off-by: Marek Vasut <marex@denx.de>
Cc: Fabio Estevam <festevam@denx.de>
Cc: Peng Fan <peng.fan@nxp.com>
Cc: Shawn Guo <shawnguo@kernel.org>
Cc: NXP Linux Team <linux-imx@nxp.com>
To: linux-arm-kernel@lists.infradead.org
Signed-off-by: Shawn Guo <shawnguo@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The I2C2 bus was initially configured to operate at a frequency of 320 kHz, which exceeds the maximum operational capability of the connected SMBus device, SMSC USB2514Bi, that can only function correctly at up to 100 kHz. This mismatch in frequency could lead to communication failures or incorrect operation of the device.

Here is the patch:
 &i2c2 {
 	/* IMX8MM ERRATA e7805 -- I2C is limited to 384 kHz due to SoC bug */
-	clock-frequency = <320000>;
+	clock-frequency = <100000>;
 	pinctrl-names = "default", "gpio";
 	pinctrl-0 = <&pinctrl_i2c2>;

Reason:
The patch reduces the I2C2 bus frequency to 100 kHz, which is within the operational limits of the SMSC USB2514Bi device, ensuring that it can communicate correctly and function as intended.
